newsitem.title: ALBANIA: IMF urges Albania to control pyramid schemes.
newsitem.headline: IMF urges Albania to control pyramid schemes.

text.p: The World Bank and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) have urged Albania to impose strict controls on suspected pyramid schemes and accelerate the privatisation of banks, the finance minister said on Monday.

"In the meetings I had (in Washington this weekend) I heard objections on some phenomena of the economy such as the banking sector privatisation and the circulation of money outside formal channels," Finance Minister Ridvan Bode told Albanian state television.
Albania set up a two-tier banking system in 1992 after the conservative government of President Sali Berisha took office, with the Bank of Albania overseeing the country's three commercial banks.
Two of the state-owned banks are now in the process of being sold off.

Bode, a former customs chief who was made finance minister in July, acknowleged pyramid schemes were an economic reality in Albania, but vowed the government would take measures to control such networks.
Numerous Albanian companies offer returns of eight to 10 percent a month on money lent to them for periods of up to three months. Some offer as much as 25 percent a month.
Bode said it was up to investors to judge the viability of such schemes. He added the returns offered were so big that they raised doubts about the company's capacity eventually to repay the loans.
"We will very soon set up the legal context to oversee this network and formalise it to minimise the risk of (potential) bankruptcy," Bode said.
